title: Weybridge and Shepperton
question: Can the guns stop them?
light: warm sun from the east, crisp black shadows

hill.described: a deserted road running down Maybury Hill at dawn in 1894 between garden walls and villas with shaven chimney tops, things dropped on the gravel as people ran, a horseless cart heeled over on a broken wheel at the corner, a smashed cash box thrown under it, the lodge of the Orphanage smoking far down the road, level country beyond out to a low flat horizon; the light is the low grey-gold dawn from the east at the RIGHT, so the road reads pale and the shadows of the walls lie long and black across it
hill.landmark: the horseless cart heeled over at the corner
hill.landmark_size: is a tenth of the height of the frame
hill.route: from the top of the road down the hill past the cart
hill.geometry: The pale road runs from the BOTTOM CENTRE down the hill away to the CENTRE, garden walls line it along the LEFT third and the RIGHT third, the heeled-over cart stands at the corner at the RIGHT third, dropped things lie on the gravel across the BOTTOM third, and the level country and low flat horizon cross the TOP third with the dawn sky above it at the TOP edge.

woods.described: a clearing in a pine wood near Maybury on a still Sunday morning in 1894: felled and trimmed pine trunks lying in rows, heaps of pale sawdust by a sawing machine and its engine, a small deserted wooden hut, tall straight pine stems all round with dark brown needles, a stack of trimmed branches by the hut, and a sandy road beyond the trees at the far side; the light is the morning sun low from the east at the LEFT through the stems, so the sawdust reads gold and the pine shadows lie black across the clearing
woods.landmark: the sawing machine and its heap of sawdust
woods.landmark_size: is a fifth of the height of the frame
woods.route: from the felled logs through the pine stems to the sandy road
woods.geometry: The felled pine trunks lie in rows across the BOTTOM third, the sawing machine and its heap of pale sawdust stand at the CENTRE LEFT, the small wooden hut stands at the RIGHT third, and tall straight pine stems fill the TOP half from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge, with the sandy road showing between them at the CENTRE and sun shafts slanting across from the LEFT.

weybridge.described: the village street of Weybridge on a sunny Sunday morning in 1894 in a tumult: carts, carriages and an old omnibus being loaded, black government waggons with white crosses in circles, people in their best Sunday clothes carrying boxes, a stone drinking fountain with a step at the centre, brick shops and houses along both sides with their doors standing open, and a church bell tower at the far end of the street; the light is the bright morning sun from the east at the RIGHT, so the street reads warm and the shadows under the carts read black
weybridge.landmark_size: is a fifth of the height of the frame
weybridge.route: from the foot of the street past the carts to the fountain
weybridge.geometry: The street runs from the BOTTOM CENTRE away to the CENTRE, loaded carts and a black government waggon stand along the LEFT third, the old omnibus stands at the RIGHT third, the stone drinking fountain stands at the CENTRE, people in Sunday clothes carry boxes across the BOTTOM third, and brick shop fronts line both sides up to the TOP third under a clear sky at the TOP edge.
weybridge.crowd: people in Sunday clothes loading carts, a dozen of them

bank.described: the gravel bank where the river Wey meets the Thames near Shepperton Lock at midday in 1894: a crowd of fugitives with bundles at the water's edge, a big ferryboat and rowing boats, an inn with a lawn on the far side, a man and his wife carrying a door piled with goods, the square tower of Shepperton church above the trees, flat meadows and silvery pollard willows out to a low flat horizon toward Chertsey; the light is the high warm midday sun from the LEFT, so the water reads silver and the shadows under the willows read black
bank.landmark: the square tower of Shepperton church
bank.landmark_size: is a fifth of the height of the frame
bank.route: from the gravel bank across the water to the inn lawn
bank.geometry: The gravel bank and the crowd with its bundles fill the BOTTOM third, the water runs across the CENTRE with the big ferryboat at the CENTRE LEFT and rowing boats at the CENTRE RIGHT, the inn lawn and the square church tower stand on the far side at the RIGHT third, and flat meadows with pollard willows run out to the low flat horizon across the TOP third at the LEFT.
bank.crowd: fugitives with bundles at the water's edge, a score of them

water.described: the wide flat Thames at Shepperton at midday in 1894 seen from the water's surface: grey-green water across the whole foreground with people swimming and boats drifting empty, a low reedy bank and a towing path, the square church tower and roofs of Shepperton beyond, flat meadows out to a low flat horizon; the light is the high midday sun from the LEFT, so the water reads bright and the bank reads black-green
water.landmark: the square church tower of Shepperton
water.landmark_size: is a fifth of the height of the frame
water.route: from the water's surface across the river to the towing path
water.geometry: The grey-green water fills the BOTTOM half from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge, the low reedy bank and towing path cross the CENTRE, the square church tower and the roofs of Shepperton stand at the RIGHT third, and the flat meadows and low flat horizon cross the TOP third under the bright sky at the TOP edge.

shots.frame: Wide down a deserted road on Maybury Hill at dawn, things dropped on the gravel, a horseless cart heeled over on a broken wheel at the corner, level country beyond.
shots.motion: The camera rises above the garden wall with small amplitude until the heeled-over cart already in the picture stands at the centre, travelling one short stride; the dawn light goes on spreading down the road; a torn curtain goes on stirring in a villa window.
shots.camera: on the road at a standing man's eye, a 35mm lens. The dawn comes from the east at the RIGHT; the road reads pale and the wall shadows read black
shots.at_rest: The pale road runs from the BOTTOM CENTRE down the hill away to the CENTRE, garden walls line it along the LEFT third and the RIGHT third, the heeled-over cart stands at the corner at the RIGHT third, dropped things lie on the gravel across the BOTTOM third, and the level country and low flat horizon cross the TOP third with the dawn sky above it at the TOP edge.
shots.why: Then we crept out of the house, and ran down the ill-made road.

shots.frame: Insert at dawn on a brass carriage clock, a lady's slipper and a silver spoon dropped on the pale gravel of the road.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in on the clock at the centre of the picture, travelling a hand's breadth; the long wall shadow goes on shortening across the gravel; the clock's hands go on ticking.
shots.camera: low over the road looking down, a 50mm lens. The dawn comes from the RIGHT; the brass reads gold and the gravel reads pale
shots.at_rest: A brass carriage clock, a lady's slipper and a silver spoon lie scattered at the CENTRE on the pale gravel, the long black shadow of a garden wall across the BOTTOM third, and the heeled-over cart's broken wheel at the TOP RIGHT. A torn letter lies beside the spoon at the BOTTOM LEFT, and the dawn light lies gold along the gravel from the RIGHT edge.
shots.why: Here and there were things that people had dropped -- a clock, a slipper, a silver spoon.

shots.frame: Medium close at dawn on the artilleryman (full black moustache, royal horse artillery driver's dark blue serge frock jacket with scarlet stand collar and brass buttons, hanging unbuttoned, hatless, his thick black hair falling forward over his brow) standing in the road, turned to the camera, his face still sooty, speaking low.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward him with small amplitude until his head and shoulders fill the middle of the picture, travelling a hand's breadth; he speaks and shakes his head; his hand goes on buttoning a biscuit packet into his jacket.
shots.camera: on the road level with his eyes, three paces from him, an 85mm lens. The dawn comes from the east at the RIGHT; his face reads gold and the wall reads grey
shots.at_rest: The artilleryman stands at the CENTRE on the road, turned to the camera, his open jacket and sooty face lit gold from the RIGHT, a garden wall behind him at the LEFT third and the pale road running away at the RIGHT third. His head is a third of the frame's height.
shots.why: 'It's no kindness to the right sort of wife,' he said, 'to make her a widow.'

shots.frame: Wide across a still pine clearing on a Sunday morning, felled trunks in rows, a sawing machine by its heap of sawdust, and a deserted hut.
shots.motion: The camera tracks sideways to the right past the felled trunks, a truck with small amplitude, until the sawing machine already in the picture stands at the centre, travelling one short stride; the sun shafts go on slanting through the stems; the dust goes on drifting in them.
shots.camera: in the clearing at a standing man's eye, a 35mm lens. The morning sun comes from the east at the LEFT; the sawdust reads gold and the shadows read black
shots.at_rest: The felled pine trunks lie in rows across the BOTTOM third, the sawing machine and its heap of pale sawdust stand at the CENTRE LEFT, the small wooden hut stands at the RIGHT third, and tall straight pine stems fill the TOP half from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge, with the sandy road showing between them at the CENTRE and sun shafts slanting across from the LEFT.
shots.why: There was not a breath of wind this morning, and everything was strangely still.

shots.frame: Medium in the pine wood on a Sunday morning on the narrator (neat close-trimmed dark brown moustache, spare straw boater with a black band, a dry second suit in the same mid-grey herringbone tweed) walking between the stems, turned to look back over his shoulder.
shots.motion: The camera tracks beside him among the pine stems as he walks, a follow with small amplitude, travelling one short stride; he goes on walking at a steady pace; his head goes on turning back over his shoulder.
shots.camera: among the pines level with his chest, four paces from him, a 50mm lens. The morning sun comes from the LEFT through the stems; his tweed reads grey and the stems read black
shots.at_rest: The narrator walks at the CENTRE among the pine stems, turned to look back over his shoulder, a pine trunk at the LEFT third and the felled logs at the BOTTOM third, sun shafts slanting across from the LEFT. His head is a sixth of the frame's height.
shots.why: We talked in whispers and looked now and again over our shoulders.

shots.frame: Medium through the pine stems on a Sunday morning at three hussars on horseback riding along a sandy road, a heliograph strapped to one saddle.
shots.motion: The camera pans from the pine stems across to the three hussars already in the picture until the hussars are at the centre, travelling a hand's breadth; the horses go on walking at a steady pace; the sun shafts go on flickering over them.
shots.camera: among the pines at a standing man's eye, a 50mm lens. The morning sun comes from the LEFT; the riders read dark blue and the road reads pale
shots.at_rest: Three hussars on horseback ride along the sandy road at the CENTRE, seen between the pine stems that stand at the LEFT third and the RIGHT third, a small brass heliograph on its stand strapped to one saddle, sun shafts across the road at the TOP third.
shots.why: We saw through the tree stems three cavalry soldiers riding towards Woking.

shots.frame: Medium close on the artilleryman (full black moustache, royal horse artillery driver's dark blue serge frock jacket with scarlet stand collar and brass buttons, hanging unbuttoned, hatless, his thick black hair falling forward over his brow) standing in the sandy road on a Sunday morning, saluting and reporting to an officer on horseback beside him.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame; he salutes and speaks; his free hand goes on sketching the height of the thing in the air.
shots.camera: in the road level with his eyes, three paces from him, an 85mm lens. The morning sun comes from the LEFT; his face reads warm and the stems read black
shots.at_rest: The artilleryman stands at the CENTRE in the sandy road, saluting with his right hand at his brow, a horse's dark flank at the RIGHT edge and pine stems behind him at the LEFT third. His head is a third of the frame's height.
shots.why: 'Giants in armour, sir. Hundred feet high. Three legs and a body like 'luminium.'

shots.frame: Medium close from the road on the narrator (neat close-trimmed dark brown moustache, spare straw boater with a black band, a dry second suit in the same mid-grey herringbone tweed) standing on the bank above it on a Sunday morning, answering down to an officer on horseback.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame from below; he speaks and nods; his hand goes on pointing south over the treetops.
shots.camera: a low angle from the road looking up at the bank, three paces from him, an 85mm lens. The morning sun comes from the LEFT; his boater reads straw and the stems read black
shots.at_rest: The narrator stands at the CENTRE on the bank above the road, his straw boater lit by the sun from the LEFT, pine stems behind him at the LEFT third and the RIGHT third. His head is a third of the frame's height.
shots.why: 'It's perfectly true,' I said.

shots.frame: Wide down the village street of Weybridge on a sunny Sunday morning in a tumult, carts and an old omnibus being loaded, people in their best clothes carrying boxes.
shots.motion: The camera rises above the carts with small amplitude until the stone drinking fountain already in the picture stands at the centre, travelling one short stride; the people go on loading the carts; a horse goes on tossing its head.
shots.camera: in the street at a standing man's eye, a 35mm lens. The morning sun comes from the east at the RIGHT; the street reads warm and the shadows under the carts read black
shots.at_rest: The street runs from the BOTTOM CENTRE away to the CENTRE, loaded carts and a black government waggon stand along the LEFT third, the old omnibus stands at the RIGHT third, the stone drinking fountain stands at the CENTRE, people in Sunday clothes carry boxes across the BOTTOM third, and brick shop fronts line both sides up to the TOP third under a clear sky at the TOP edge.
shots.why: Byfleet was in a tumult; people packing, and a score of hussars hunting them about.

shots.frame: Medium on four grenadiers in white fatigue jackets among the loaded carts on a sunny Sunday morning, waving the people on.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward the grenadiers already in the picture with small amplitude, travelling a hand's breadth; the grenadiers go on waving the people on; the people go on carrying their boxes past.
shots.camera: in the street at a standing man's eye, a 50mm lens. The morning sun comes from the RIGHT; the jackets read white and the waggon reads black
shots.at_rest: Four grenadiers in white fatigue jackets stand at the CENTRE among the loaded carts, waving people on, a black government waggon at the LEFT third and people in Sunday clothes with boxes at the RIGHT third. An old omnibus stands behind them at the TOP third, and a dropped hatbox lies in the street at the BOTTOM LEFT. The brick shop fronts rise behind the carts to the TOP edge, and the morning sun lies warm across the cobbles from the RIGHT edge.
shots.why: The soldiers were having the greatest difficulty in making them realise the gravity of their position.

shots.frame: Medium in the sunny street on an old man in a black coat beside a huge wooden box with pots of orchids on its lid, pointing at them and arguing.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame; he goes on pointing at his orchids; his other hand goes on waving.
shots.camera: in the street at a standing man's eye, a 50mm lens. The morning sun comes from the RIGHT; the orchids read pink and the coat reads black
shots.at_rest: An old man in a black coat stands at the CENTRE beside a huge wooden box with pots of orchids on its lid, pointing at them, a loaded cart behind him at the LEFT third and the brick shop fronts at the RIGHT third. A grenadier in a white fatigue jacket stands behind him at the TOP LEFT, and more pots of orchids stand on the cobbles at the BOTTOM RIGHT.
shots.why: One shrivelled old fellow with a huge box and a score of flower pots containing orchids.

shots.frame: Close in the sunny street on the narrator (neat close-trimmed dark brown moustache, spare straw boater with a black band, a dry second suit in the same mid-grey herringbone tweed) gripping an old man's black sleeve and shouting into his face, pointing past him at the far pine tops.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward his face with small amplitude until it fills the middle of the picture, travelling a hand's breadth; he shouts; his arm goes on pointing at the pine tops.
shots.camera: in the street level with his eyes, two paces from him, an 85mm lens. The morning sun comes from the RIGHT; his face reads warm and the street reads bright
shots.at_rest: The narrator fills the CENTRE, gripping an old man's black sleeve at the BOTTOM LEFT with one hand and pointing past the camera with the other, his mouth open, the street behind him at the RIGHT third. His head is half the frame's height.
shots.why: 'Death!' I shouted. 'Death is coming! Death!'

shots.frame: Insert in the sunny street on two hands breaking a slice of bread and meat over a plain brown paper wrapping on the stone step of a drinking fountain.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in on the bread at the centre of the picture, travelling a hand's breadth; the hands go on breaking the bread; the shadows of passing carts go on sliding over the step.
shots.camera: above the step looking down, a 50mm lens. The morning sun comes from the RIGHT; the bread reads pale and the stone reads grey
shots.at_rest: Two hands break a slice of bread and meat at the CENTRE over a plain brown paper wrapping on the pale stone step of the drinking fountain, a grey herringbone tweed cuff at the LEFT third and the fountain's basin rim across the TOP third. The shadow of a passing cart wheel crosses the step at the RIGHT third, and crumbs lie on the stone at the BOTTOM edge.
shots.why: Seated on the step of the drinking fountain, we made a very passable meal.

shots.frame: Wide at midday over the gravel bank where the Wey meets the Thames, a crowd of fugitives with bundles at the water, the big ferryboat crossing, the church tower above the trees.
shots.motion: The camera pans from the crowd across to the big ferryboat already in the picture until the ferryboat is at the centre, travelling a hand's breadth; the ferryboat goes on crossing; the crowd goes on pressing to the water.
shots.camera: on the gravel bank at a standing man's eye, a 35mm lens. The midday sun comes from the LEFT; the water reads silver and the willows read black
shots.at_rest: The gravel bank and the crowd with its bundles fill the BOTTOM third, the water runs across the CENTRE with the big ferryboat at the CENTRE LEFT and rowing boats at the CENTRE RIGHT, the inn lawn and the square church tower stand on the far side at the RIGHT third, and flat meadows with pollard willows run out to the low flat horizon across the TOP third at the LEFT.
shots.why: There were already far more people than all the boats going to and fro could enable to cross.

shots.frame: Insert at midday over the flat meadows toward Chertsey on a single white puff of smoke jerking up above the far trees, cows grazing below.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward the puff of smoke already in the picture with small amplitude, travelling a hand's breadth; the puff of smoke goes on rising and hanging; the cows go on grazing.
shots.camera: on the bank looking up the river, a 135mm lens. The midday sun comes from the LEFT; the smoke reads white and the meadows read green
shots.at_rest: A single white puff of smoke hangs above the far trees at the CENTRE, small against the sky, the flat meadows with cows and pollard willows across the BOTTOM half and the low flat horizon at the CENTRE. A line of silvery pollard willows crosses the BOTTOM third from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge, and a haze hangs over the far trees at the TOP third.
shots.why: Then suddenly we saw a rush of smoke far away up the river.

shots.frame: Medium at midday across the flat meadows at four armoured tripods far off, striding toward the river with a rolling motion, glittering in the sun.
shots.motion: The camera tracks sideways to the left past the pollard willows, a truck with small amplitude, until the four tripods already in the picture stand at the centre, travelling one short stride; the four tripods go on striding toward the river; the willows go on sliding by in the foreground.
shots.camera: on the bank at a standing man's eye, a 50mm lens. The midday sun comes from the LEFT and glitters on the metal; the tripods read silver and the meadows read green
shots.at_rest: Four tall armoured tripods stride across the flat meadows at the CENTRE, far off, each a sixth of the height of the frame, glittering in the sun, the pollard willows along the BOTTOM third and the low flat horizon behind them. Cows graze in the meadow at the BOTTOM LEFT, and a thin haze of smoke rises over the far trees at the TOP RIGHT.
shots.why: One, two, three, four of the armoured Martians appeared, striding hurriedly towards the river.

shots.frame: Medium close at midday on the narrator (neat close-trimmed dark brown moustache, spare straw boater with a black band, a dry second suit in the same mid-grey herringbone tweed) at the water's edge, turned to the fleeing crowd and shouting, the river behind him.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame; he shouts to the crowd with his mouth wide open; his arm goes on sweeping toward the water.
shots.camera: on the gravel level with his eyes, three paces from him, an 85mm lens. The midday sun comes from the LEFT; his face reads warm and the river reads silver
shots.at_rest: The narrator stands at the CENTRE at the water's edge, turned to the crowd and shouting, his straw boater pushed back, the river behind him at the TOP third and people running at the RIGHT third. His head is half the frame's height.
shots.turn: a man walking away from it -> a man running into the river toward it
shots.why: 'Get under water!' I shouted, unheeded.

shots.frame: Medium at midday on the narrator (neat close-trimmed dark brown moustache, a dry second suit in the same mid-grey herringbone tweed) seen from behind, running waist-deep into the river toward the far bank, splashes flying around him.
shots.motion: The camera tracks behind him into the water as he runs, a follow with small amplitude, travelling one short stride; he goes on running through the water at a hard pace; his arms go on throwing forward.
shots.camera: at the water's edge behind him at a standing man's eye, four paces from him, a 35mm lens. The midday sun comes from the LEFT; the splashes read white and his coat reads grey
shots.at_rest: The narrator runs away from the camera at the CENTRE, waist-deep in the river, his arms thrown forward, splashes around him, the far bank and the church tower at the TOP third.
shots.why: I faced about again, and rushed right down the gravelly beach and headlong into the water.

shots.frame: Medium from the river's surface at midday up at a tall tripod wading across the Thames, its hood swinging toward the unseen batteries.
shots.motion: The camera tilts up from the water to the tripod already in the picture until the tripod stands in the middle of the frame, travelling a forearm; the tripod goes on wading across the river; the water goes on churning round its legs.
shots.camera: a low angle from the water's surface looking up, a 24mm lens. The midday sun comes from the LEFT; the tripod reads silver and the water reads green
shots.at_rest: A tall tripod wades the river at the CENTRE, seen from the water's surface, its three legs reaching from the water at the BOTTOM third to its hooded body at the TOP third, the church tower of Shepperton at the RIGHT third. The water churns white round its legs at the BOTTOM third, and the far bank with its reeds crosses the CENTRE from the LEFT edge.
shots.why: In another moment it was on the bank, and in a stride wading halfway across.

shots.frame: Insert at midday on the brass hood of a tripod bursting apart in a white flash and a round ball of grey smoke as a shell strikes it, three large torn brass plates falling away against the bright sky above the Thames.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward the bursting hood already in the picture with small amplitude, travelling a hand's breadth; the torn plates go on falling away; the smoke goes on spreading.
shots.camera: from the river looking up, a 135mm lens. The midday sun comes from the LEFT; the flash reads white and the metal reads gold
shots.at_rest: The brass hood of a tripod fills the CENTRE, bursting apart in a white flash and a round ball of grey smoke, three large torn brass plates falling away to the LEFT third and the RIGHT third against the bright sky. Grey smoke spreads from the burst across the TOP third, and the tripod's white body hangs below the hood at the BOTTOM third.
shots.why: The shell burst clean in the face of the Thing.

shots.frame: Close at midday on the face of the narrator (neat close-trimmed dark brown moustache, a dry second suit in the same mid-grey herringbone tweed) chest-deep in the river, soaked, crying out with his arms up.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame; he cries out; his head goes on tipping back with the shout.
shots.camera: at the water's surface level with his eyes, two paces from him, an 85mm lens. The midday sun comes from the LEFT; his wet face reads bright and the water reads green
shots.at_rest: The narrator's face fills the CENTRE, chest-deep in the river, water streaming from his hair, his mouth open in a cry, the bright water at the BOTTOM third. His head is half the frame's height.
shots.why: 'Hit!' shouted I, with something between a scream and a cheer.

shots.frame: Wide at midday on the headless tripod reeling across Shepperton, striking the square church tower down, and a spout of steam and water leaping from the river.
shots.motion: The camera pans from the steam across to the church tower already in the picture until the tower is at the centre, travelling a hand's breadth; the tower goes on breaking apart; the steam goes on leaping up.
shots.camera: at the water's surface, a 35mm lens. The midday sun comes from the LEFT; the steam reads white and the tower reads grey
shots.at_rest: The headless tripod reels at the CENTRE, one leg striking the square church tower at the RIGHT third, the tower breaking apart, and a tall white spout of steam and water rising from the river at the LEFT third. Broken masonry falls from the tower at the RIGHT edge, and the grey water heaves across the BOTTOM third. The roofs of Shepperton stand along the TOP third, and empty boats pitch on the waves at the BOTTOM LEFT.
shots.why: It struck the tower of Shepperton Church, smashing it down.

shots.frame: Medium close at midday on the artilleryman (full black moustache, royal horse artillery driver's dark blue serge frock jacket with scarlet stand collar and brass buttons, hanging unbuttoned, hatless, his thick black hair falling forward over his brow) knee-deep at the river's edge, turned to the camera, white steam rising behind him.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame; he speaks bitterly; his hand goes on wiping the water from his face.
shots.camera: at the water's edge level with his eyes, three paces from him, an 85mm lens. The midday sun comes from the LEFT; his face reads warm and the steam reads white
shots.at_rest: The artilleryman stands at the CENTRE on the gravel bank, turned to the camera, water to his knees, white steam rising behind him at the TOP third and the crowd fleeing at the LEFT third. His head is a third of the frame's height.
shots.why: 'It's bows and arrows against the lightning, anyhow.'

shots.frame: Wide at midday over the river filled with white steam, four grey tripods standing huge and dim in it, the boiling water rolling toward a gravel spit.
shots.motion: The camera rises above the water with small amplitude until the four tripods already in the picture stand at the centre, travelling one short stride; the steam goes on rolling across the river; the four tripods go on striding through it.
shots.camera: at the water's surface, a 35mm lens. The midday sun comes from the LEFT through the steam; the steam reads white and the tripods read grey
shots.at_rest: White steam fills the TOP half above the river, four tall grey tripods standing in it at the CENTRE, dim and huge, the boiling water across the BOTTOM third and the gravel spit at the BOTTOM LEFT. Heads of people in the water show at the BOTTOM RIGHT, and the burning roofs of Weybridge glow through the steam at the LEFT edge.
shots.why: Then I saw them dimly, colossal figures of grey, magnified by the mist.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: At dawn we crept out and down the road I had driven overnight.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: People had dropped things as they ran. A clock. A slipper. A silver spoon.

lines.speaker: artilleryman
lines.text: It's no kindness to the right sort of wife, to make her a widow.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: In the pine woods, not a breath of wind. Even the birds were hushed.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: We talked in whispers, and kept looking back over our shoulders.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Through the trees, three hussars were riding toward Woking. We hailed them.

lines.speaker: artilleryman
lines.text: Giants in armour, sir. A hundred feet high.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: It is perfectly true.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Weybridge was in a tumult. Everyone packing, and in their Sunday best.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The soldiers could not make them understand what was coming.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: One shrivelled old fellow would not leave his pots of orchids behind.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Death is coming! Death!

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: We ate what we had brought, on the step of the drinking fountain.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: By noon we were at Shepperton, where the Wey meets the Thames. Too few boats.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: A gun thudded toward Chertsey. Then a puff of smoke, far up the river.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: One, two, three, four of them, striding across the meadows to the river.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Get under the water!

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I turned and ran headlong into the river, toward the thing.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: It waded halfway across. Then the six hidden guns at Shepperton fired together.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: A shell burst clean in its face, and the brass hood flew apart.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Hit! They have hit it!

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Headless, it reeled on, struck down the church tower, and fell.

lines.speaker: artilleryman
lines.text: It is bows and arrows against the lightning, anyhow.
